rationale: C04 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both directives authorize a military department secretary to confer an honor in the President's name, define eligibility based on qualifying combat action, prescribe an additional device for subsequent qualifying awards, and conclude by superseding an earlier directive. This combination of parallel operative machinery and closely shared language is materially stronger than the general military-awards similarities in C06 and C09.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Secretaries of the Army, the Navy, and the Air Force, respectively, are hereby authorized to issue a citation in the name of the President of the United States
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Secretary of the Navy shall award the Purple Heart, in the name of the President of the United States
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same secretary-administered mechanism for issuing a military honor expressly in the President's name.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Such persons are authorized to wear an appropriate additional device for any subsequent citation for which they are eligible
shared_material.parent_excerpt: for each subsequent justification for such an award a Gold Star, or other suitable device, shall be awarded to be worn with the Purple Heart
shared_material.explanation: Both establish a wearable additional device to represent subsequent qualifying honors.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This order supersedes [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of February 6, 1942, and No. 9396 of November 22, 1943.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This order shall supersede [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of December 3, 1941, entitled "Award of the Purple Heart to Persons Serving with the Navy, Marine Corps or Coast Guard of the United States"
shared_material.explanation: Each consolidates or replaces prior military-award authority through an express supersession provision.
